mainText:
Fonterra lifts its farmgate milk price forecast to nine dollars seventy five, and Netball New Zealand scraps the proposed Mowbray-Williams private league, throwing next year's competition into doubt.

New Zealand.

Netball New Zealand has ended its agreement for a proposed private league backed by Jenny-May Mowbray-Williams, eight weeks after signing a term sheet. It leaves the structure of next year's competition unresolved. Silver Ferns coach Dame Noeline Taurua has separately dropped the mandatory Yo-Yo fitness test after seven years, replacing it with a tailored, role-specific conditioning model designed by performance director Amanda Murphy.

Fonterra has raised its twenty twenty six, twenty seven farmgate milk price forecast to nine dollars seventy five per kilogram of milksolids, up twenty five cents, citing stronger milk powder demand. The lift benefits dairying regions nationwide. Separately, Precinct Properties has shelved its nine hundred million dollar downtown Auckland development and will delay its Downtown Carpark project, returning one hundred and eight million dollars to shareholders on Friday the thirteenth of November.

Pak'nSave stores in Hamilton and Auckland's Silverdale have been fined five hundred and eighty thousand, five hundred dollars after admitting eighteen fair trading charges for charging more at the till than shelf prices showed.

Provisional voter enrolment stands at ninety three point six percent, below the ninety four point seven percent recorded at the twenty twenty three election, the Electoral Commission says. Early voting has soared above twenty twenty three levels, with hundreds of thousands casting ballots in the first three days. Election day is November the seventh.

A Fire and Emergency training report has found major flaws in firefighter instruction, including a disputed claim that an old-style military approach was used to belittle recruits. The report calls the training outdated, disjointed and unsafe.

In Western Bay of Plenty, Alan Kurtovich has confirmed his council resignation was driven by the district's Māori wards decision, the trigger for the byelection now under way. In Kawerau, Dallas Hohua, convicted of manslaughter for stabbing a friend to death after a party, may now serve as little as two years after his sentence was reduced.

Snow has closed Arthur's Pass and Lewis Pass, with thunderstorms, hail and lightning possible across both islands today, MetService says.

World.

Britain's Chancellor John Healey faces fallout from his first Budget, with think tanks warning of painful years ahead as living standards growth grinds almost to a halt. Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says he wants the welfare bill cut "as soon as we possibly can," though no timetable has been set.

Israel's election count is complete. Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud bloc and allies have fifty three of one hundred and twenty Knesset seats, short of a majority. Netanyahu has accused Palestinian-Israeli parties of trying to "delegitimise" the result, as opposition parties explore joining forces with them to form a government.

A Russian drone attack on a train station in Dnipro, central Ukraine, has killed at least fourteen people and wounded others, including an eleven year old boy, officials say.

Alphabet lost half a trillion dollars in market value in its worst single trading day on record, as investors weigh tensions in the company's shift from search engine to artificial intelligence hyperscaler.

Technology.

Anthropic's initial public offering prospectus has disclosed further detail on the company, including a warning of what it calls catastrophic risk from artificial intelligence, as it prepares to become the first major AI company to list publicly. A global cyber security scramble over a flaw in the PHP programming language, uncovered with the help of artificial intelligence tools, continues several days on. Britain's government is investing one hundred million pounds in a new AI biosecurity lab to address emerging risks.

Sport.

Cricket. Black Caps batter Bevon Jacobs returns to a sold out Eden Park for the final Twenty20 against India on Friday night. Lockie Ferguson is out of the rest of the series with a low grade calf tear. In the test series decider in Cape Town, Australia are closing in on victory over South Africa after Nathan Lyon dismissed the Proteas captain and careless batting from the top order.

Rugby. All Blacks coach Dave Rennie is still chasing the consistency and ruthlessness of his previous sides on the northern tour. Recalled Crusaders forward Leicester Fainga'anuku says he is ready to use his versatility after being named in a hybrid loose forward role. The Black Ferns have made multiple changes for their final test of the year against France in Christchurch. New Zealand Rugby has confirmed Super Rugby and the NPC will both continue next year, though job losses are expected in the main centres as the body seeks cost savings.

Netball. The Silver Ferns' dominant season ended in a loss to the Australian Diamonds in their final hit out before next year's World Cup. Captain Karin Burger says the result does not make them favourites.

Formula One. Liam Lawson hands his car to Formula Two driver Nikola Tsolov for an hour of practice at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend, part of Tsolov's audition for a future drive. Kimi Antonelli will miss Thursday's media day in Mexico City with illness, as he stands on the brink of his first world title.

Boxing. A world title fight has opened up as an option for Joseph Parker's return to the ring, New Zealand heavyweight boxing's governing bodies have yet to confirm an opponent.

Golf. The Asia Pacific Amateur continues at Te Arai, with New Zealand's Zack Swanwick leading the home challenge. Places at next year's Masters and the Open Championship are on offer to the leading finishers.

Coming up. The Black Caps play India at Eden Park on Friday night. The Mexican Grand Prix runs this weekend. The Black Ferns play France in Christchurch. Election day is November the seventh.

End of flash.
